findings.body:
`subprocess.run` is switched to `shell=True` while building the command with an f-string over `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`. Those values are passed straight to the shell, so metacharacters are executed.

**Failure mode:** `name` (or `upload_dir` / `oid`) containing shell metacharacters runs arbitrary commands as the worker user, e.g. `name = "img.png; id > /tmp/pwned"` becomes two commands. The previous argv-list form did not have this behavior. Upstream validation is not present in this repo, and even a filename allowlist would not cover `upload_dir` or `oid`.

ImageMagick policy delegates do not require a shell — keep list-form exec:

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

If IM7 needs the `magick` binary, use `["/usr/bin/magick", "convert", src, dst]` (still list form, still absolute path).

The command now resolves `convert` via `PATH` instead of `/usr/bin/convert`. On a shared or compromised runner, an earlier PATH entry can shadow the real binary and execute attacker-controlled code whenever thumbnails are generated.

Restore an absolute path (or `magick` under `/usr/bin`) in list-form argv so the binary location does not depend on ambient PATH.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces shell command injection in thumbnail conversion.

## Narrative

`make_thumb` previously invoked ImageMagick via argv-list form (`subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/convert", src, dst])`), which does not pass arguments through a shell. The PR switches to `shell=True` and interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` directly into the command string.

Any metacharacters in those values (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, spaces, etc.) are interpreted by the shell. A crafted `name` such as `x; id > /tmp/pwned` (or similar in `upload_dir` / `oid`) runs arbitrary commands as the process user. The removed comment claimed upstream `ALLOWED_FILES` validation for `name` only; this repo has no such validator in-tree, and `upload_dir` / `oid` were never covered by that claim anyway.

The stated rationale ("shell form needed for the imagemagick policy delegate") does not hold: ImageMagick 7 policy/delegate configuration is enforced inside the `convert`/`magick` binary regardless of how the process is spawned. If IM7 requires the `magick` binary or a different argv, keep the list form (and preferably the absolute path `/usr/bin/convert` or `/usr/bin/magick`).

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The change replaces safe list-form subprocess.run with shell=True and an f-string that interpolates upload_dir, name, and oid unquoted, enabling classic shell metacharacter injection. Base used argv list form; no in-repo validation of those parameters exists.
